verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is community mention of Bitbucket's own deploy keys, which are read-only and can be attached to multiple repos. This implies key-based (SSH) read access for cloning and pulling, and the docs reference commits feeding Jira updates, which implies pushing. No first-party documentation describes cloning, pulling, or pushing over HTTPS or SSH with standard Git clients. Missing for 10: documented HTTPS clone/push support, documented SSH clone/push setup, explicit push workflow evidence, standard Git client compatibility statement, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can clone, pull, and push repositories with any standard Git client over HTTPS or SSH

citations.quote: Bitbucket's deploy keys fit typical use better than GitHub's. They are read-only and one key can be attached to multiple repos
